question.text: This province is the most populous and borders both Minnesota and New York. The capital Ottawa and the major city of Toronto both lie in this province.
question.clue: The First Nations leader Tecumseh was killed in this province during the Battle of the Thames (TIMS) in the War of 1812.

swap.text: The Iroquois fought against Huron and Algonquin natives, as well as French trappers, in a series of wars thatare named for this dam-building animal, a primary target of French fur traders in the area.

question.text: This man was the first Prime Minister of Canada. He served in two separate terms after resigning due to the Pacific Railway Scandal, which saw Tory politicians bribed to give out prime rail routes.
question.clue: In the Great Coalition, this man joined George-Etienne Cartier and George Brown at the Charlottetown Conference to push for confederation.

swap.leadin: Prime Ministers from this party have included John Major and Margaret Thatcher.
swap.text: Name this British political party, the biggest rival of the Labour Party.
swap.clue: Although Chamberlain was succeeded as Prime Minister by Winston Churchill, he remained leader of this political party, to which both he and Churchill belonged.

question.text: This 1774 act allowed the free practice of Catholicism in its namesake colony, and also defined the boundary for that colony.
question.clue: This act was one of the intolerable acts. It allowed freedom of religion in Canada and granted the namesake colony land west of the Appalachian.

swap.text: This Canadian unifying event consisted of three different uprisings including the Patriot War. This event led to the merger of Lower and Upper Canada into a single government and to the issuing of the Durham report.
swap.clue: This series of Canadian revolts which saw the Patriote movement fight British troops at Sainte-Charles and Sainte Eustache during the namesake year.

question.leadin: This conflict began after the kidnapping of diplomat James Cross.
question.text: Name this period of unrest initiated by the Front de Liberation Quebec in 1970.
question.clue: Robert Bourassa appeared on television five minutes prior to a deadline in this event stating that his government would not negotiate, resulting in the retaliatory execution of Pierre LaPorte, who had been kidnapped along with James Cross.

swap.leadin: Accusations of vote-buying in this scandal led to the swift introduction of a secret ballot by the next government.
swap.text: Name this scandal in which Hugh Allan bribed lawmakers to win a contract to build a railroad. It led to the downfall of John Macdonald's government.
swap.clue: Shortly after this event, secret ballots were introduced and Sandford Fleming was appointed by the Department of Public Works to ensure that certain parts of an enterprise were built publicly.

question.text: He left his priesthood in 1667 to become a fur trader. Six years later, he left Saint Ignace and went across Lake Michigan to the Fox River, which he followed to the Wisconsin. Eventually going as far south as the Arkansas, he reported his findings to Governor Frontenac. For 15 points-name this explorer who mapped the upper Mississippi with Jacques Marquette.
question.clue: This man was the only survivor, as a slave from Illinois and two other men drowned, when this explorer's canoe capsized near the St. Louis Rapids.

swap.leadin: Jacques Parizeau blamed the result of this event on "money and the ethnic vote."
swap.text: Name this 1995 event, in which an unprecedented 93.5% turnout resulted in a narrow loss by 1% of the vote cast. The "Clarity Act" of 2000 made it more difficult for events like this one to occur in the future.
swap.answerHtml: 1995 Quebec independence referendum [accept descriptive answers indicating a referendum or vote on the independence of Quebec]

question.leadin: Answer the following about western exploration and settlement in America.
question.text: It's unclear how many people actually drowned fording a river while traveling on the real-life Oregon Trail, but it is clear that the most famous Oregon Trail route began in this Missouri city, which was also the hometown of Harry Truman.

swap.text: In 1970, Pierre Trudeau declared martial law in Quebec response to the October Crisis, in which British Trade Commissioner James Cross was kidnapped and provincial Labour Minister Pierre Laporte was murdered by this terrorist group.
swap.clue: Members of this group kidnapped British Trade Commissioner James Cross and Minister of Labour and Immigration Pierre Laporte.

question.text: The Treaty of Washington, which did not provide compensation for the Fenians, was a disappointment for this first Prime Minister of Canada, who later lost office for accepting bribes from the builders of the Pacific Railway.
question.clue: This Conservative who was forced to resign following the Pacific Scandal.

swap.text: In another railroad-finance affair, this Canadian prime minister lost an election to the Liberal Party after favoring the Canadian Pacific Railroad over its competitors in the Pacific Scandal.
swap.clue: One scandal that this man was involved in eventually cooled down because larger organizations in Great Britain and the United States took control of the project.

question.leadin: This leader reclassified thousands of orphans as mentally ill in order to claim extra federal subsidies for their care, leading to abuse of children in insane asylums on a massive scale.
question.text: Name this Quebecois leader who implemented a set of conservative policies called the Great Darkness before his Union Nationale Party was deposed in 1959.
question.clue: The church opposed Laurier with the slogan "Heaven is blue, hell is red," which was later taken up by this Premier of Quebec. This conservative passed the Padlock Law and presided over a period called "The Great Darkness."

swap.text: As Justice Minister, Pierre Trudeau claimed that the state had no place in one part of a home to defend this policy change, inspired by a similar law passed by Harold Wilson's government along with abortion and divorce reform.
swap.answerHtml: decriminalizing homosexual acts [accept synonyms like legalizing in place of “decriminalizing”; accept synonyms like homosexuality or “same sex relations between men” in place of “homosexual acts”]

question.leadin: Answer the following about strained racial relations in Canadian history.
question.text: This militantly anti-English group's killing of Pierre Laporte in 1970 led to the October Crisis, in which Pierre Trudeau deployed military forces to restore order.
question.answerHtml: FLQ [or Front de libération du Québec; or Quebec Liberation Front]
question.clue: The (+) South Shore Gang was a subgroup of this organization, members of which kidnapped James Cross and Pierre Laporte in an action that prompted Pierre Trudeau to invoke the War Measures Act.

swap.leadin: In 1959, this socialist released his Medicare plan, which promised to provide every person in Saskatchewan with public health care.
swap.text: Name this Baptist minister who served for seventeen years as Premier of Saskatchewan, and then led the newly-formed New Democratic Party from 1961 to 1971.
swap.clue: During a 1944 election, this politician told a fable in which the mouse constituency elects black cats and white cats but never mice in "Mouseland."

question.leadin: Answer the following about Dief the Chief.
question.text: Dief-more formally, John Diefenbaker-was the first prime minister from this Canadian political party. This center-right political party merged with the Canadian Alliance in 2003 to form the modern-day Conservative Party of Canada.
question.answerHtml: Progressive Conservative Party of Canada [or Parti progressiste-conservateur du Canada; do not accept or prompt on simply Progressive or Conservative Party]
question.clue: Diefenbaker led this right-wing party, historically one of two major parties in Canada. It lost a lot of support in the 1990s, and merged with the Canadian Alliance in 2003.

swap.text: The Social Credit party held power in this province for 36 years. As first premier of the Northwest Territories, Frederick Haultain prepared the way for its 1905 establishment.
swap.clue: Bumper stickers that read "Let the eastern bastards freeze in the dark" were popularized in this province in response to the National Energy Program of Pierre Trudeau.
